title: AnorexiaVR – Virtual Exposure Therapy for Adolescent Patients with Anorexia Nervosa
summary:
Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe psychiatric disorder that often begins in adolescence (Solmi et al., 2022). Body image disorder is a key factor in the maintenance of AN; therefore, interventions aimed at improving body image are important (Glashouwer et al., 2019). Therapeutic confrontation with one’s own body has proven helpful in reducing body-related fears (Griffen et al., 2018; Naumann et al., 2022). Unlike real-world body confrontation, virtual reality (VR) allows for the manipulation of avatar weight. Avatars are the digital representation of the self in virtual environments. Initial studies on weight modulation in VR are promising. 
Therefore, this pilot study examines a VR body exposure intervention, developed in collaboration with the Berliner Hochschule für Technik (BHT), for inpatient female adolescents with AN (F50.0), with regard to patient-centered feasibility, acceptance, and satisfaction (primary outcomes), as well as eating disorder psychopathology, embodiment, and motion sickness (exploratory secondary outcomes).

interventions.name: Body exposure in virtual reality with gradual weight gain of a personalized avatar for adolescent female patients diagnosed with anorexia nervosa (ICD-10: F50.0), as a supplement to inpatient multimodal treatment for eating disorders. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (F50.0) according to ICD-10, confirmed by the Eating Disorder Examination (EDE; Hilbert, 2016)
- Inpatient treatment
- Ability to provide informed consent to participate in the study: participants and legal guardians
- Ability to complete the questionnaires: participants
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language: participants and legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
- Physical conditions that, due to their nature and severity, could interfere with the planned examinations or affect the parameters being studied (e.g., Visually Induced Motion Sickness (VIMS))
- Impaired vision, lack of depth perception, color blindness
- Insufficient knowledge of the German language
- Pregnancy
- Severe psychiatric comorbidities (e.g., psychotic disorders, bipolar disorders)
- Acute suicidal ideation
